brief:
Ibrahim Said cast his ballot in Israeli elections for the first time since 1980, breaking a long personal boycott of a political process most Palestinians view as delegitimizing Israeli rule over occupied territories. Said's decision to vote reflects a strategic shift among some Palestinians within Israel who see electoral participation as essential to protecting their communities' basic interests and survival, according to Middle East Eye.

The move marks a departure from the broader Palestinian political stance of rejecting Israeli elections as incompatible with resistance to occupation. Palestinians in Israel, who hold Israeli citizenship, have historically faced pressure to boycott voting as a form of protest against the state's control of Palestinian lands and governance.

title: Palestinians vote in Israel despite decades of boycott calls
